title: The Sword and the Dollar
author: Michael Parenti
desc: Relación entre poder militar y poder económico en la política exterior de EE.UU.
tesis: La espada y el dólar van juntos: la política exterior de Estados Unidos no busca 'democracia' ni 'seguridad nacional' sino proteger las inversiones y los mercados de las corporaciones estadounidenses. Parenti traza cómo el aparato militar sirve directamente a los intereses económicos de la clase dominante — desde las intervenciones en Centroamérica hasta el apoyo a dictaduras pro-empresariales en todo el Tercer Mundo.
ideas: La política exterior de EE.UU. protege inversiones corporativas, no derechos humanos ni democracia.
Las intervenciones militares en el Tercer Mundo siguen un patrón: derrocar gobiernos nacionalistas, imponer regímenes pro-corporativos.
El presupuesto militar no es 'defensa' sino subsidio público masivo al complejo industrial-militar.
contexto: Publicado en 1989 por St. Martin's Press, durante las guerras encubiertas de Reagan en Centroamérica. Parenti escribió el libro mientras EE.UU. financiaba contras en Nicaragua y escuadrones de la muerte en El Salvador, demostrando exactamente su tesis sobre la relación entre poder militar y capital corporativo.

conexiones.razon: The Sword and the Dollar expone los mecanismos; Against Empire analiza el sistema completo.
Galeano narra los efectos en América Latina de la política de espada y dólar que Parenti desmonta.

tl: Revolución de Octubre

When the workers, under the leadership of Lenin's Bolshevik party, seized power in Russia in 1917, the working people of America expressed neither fright nor hysteria; indeed, many worker organizations offered expressions of solidarity. But the fear was palpable among the owning classes of this and other capitalist nations.
The Cold War Is an Old War
Quince potencias capitalistas invaden la Rusia soviética

Beginning in August 1918, fourteen nations, including the United States, Great Britain, France, and Japan invaded Soviet Russia in an attempt to overthrow the Bolshevik government. In addition to using their own troops, they provided aid to the reactionary pro-czarist White Guard generals.
The Cold War Is an Old War
Marines reprimen elecciones en Nicaragua

In 1986, Bill Gandall, aged seventy-seven, recalled how in 1928 he spent two years as a Marine in Nicaragua fighting Augusto Cesar Sandino, the leader for whom the Sandinistas are named: 'We never caught him because no matter how we tortured, we could never get people to inform.' He remembers how the Marine Corps spread democracy in Nicaragua: 'I shot a guy at the polls' in the fraudulent election of 1928.
Imperial State Terrorism
Embargo occidental contra la República Española

While Hitler and Mussolini sent troops and armaments to help the fascist General Franco crush the Spanish Republic in 1936-39, the United States, Great Britain, and France maintained an embargo against that beleaguered democracy, effectively contributing to its defeat. The Soviet Union and Mexico were the only nations to aid the Republic.
Between Two Wars and Two Worlds
Truman lanza la bomba atómica pensando en Moscú

On the eve of the first atomic test, before Potsdam and long before the Soviet 'threats' that supposedly led to the cold war, President Truman's first thoughts were of the Russians: 'If [the atomic bomb] explodes, as I think it will, I'll certainly have a hammer on those boys.' ... Thus, a monster bomb, developed by European refugees to defeat Hitler, was dropped by Americans on the Japanese mostly in order to intimidate the Russians.
Between Two Wars and Two Worlds
Plan Baruch ofrece monopolio nuclear a EE. UU.

In 1946, the US proposed the Baruch Plan, setting up an international commission, on which the United States would enjoy a controlling majority. The commission would have exclusive command of all atomic research, raw materials, and industries throughout the world. ... As Secretary of State Dean Acheson wrote, the American proposal was 'almost certain to wreck any possibility of Russian acceptance.'
Can We Trust the Russians?
Golpe contra Arbenz en Guatemala

After it expropriated some uncultivated lands belonging to the United Fruit Company, the democratically elected Arbenz government in Guatemala was overthrown in 1953 by a mercenary force financed and directed by the CIA. According to a former United Fruit Company official, 'United Fruit was involved at every level' in the planning and execution of the coup.
Against Imperialism
Golpe en Indonesia: entre medio millón y un millón de muertos

The recipients of about $2 billion in US military and economic aid over the last ten years, the Indonesian generals came to power in a coup that took the lives of 500,000 to 1 million people in 1965. A decade later, the generals conducted a war of attrition against East Timor, a former Portuguese colony which upon independence had chosen a populist socialist government.
Imperial State Terrorism
EE. UU. despliega misiles MIRV antes que la URSS

The US had MIRVs in 1970, the Soviets in 1975. As of 1988, the US had built cruise missiles and maneuverable re-entry vehicles (MARVs), while the Soviets had yet to develop such weapons. ... In 1970, the Soviets made twenty-six separate overtears to limit the deployment of MIRV missiles.
The Arms Chase
Golpe contra Allende en septiembre de 1973

The Pinochet military dictatorship that murdered Allende and seized power in Chile in 1973 abolished all political liberties, executed about 30,000 Chileans, and arrested, tortured, or drove into exile many thousands more. Pinochet's free-market policies, formulated by conservative economists from the USA, brought runaway inflation, a drastic drop in real wages, a sharp growth in unemployment, deep cuts in human services, and a huge increase in the national debt.
The Mean Methods of Imperialism (II)
Doctrina Carter sobre el petróleo del Golfo
In 1979, in what became known as the Carter Doctrine, President Carter proclaimed, in so many words, a readiness to go to war with anyone who tampered with US-owned oil in the Middle East.
Other Variables—or Must We Ignore Imperialism?
Masacre del Mozote en El Salvador

On December 11, 1981, a US-trained elite battalion killed more than 1,000 people in the village of Mozote and some nearby hamlets. The survivors fled into the forest and five years later they were still in hiding, subjected to constant aerial attacks.
Imperial State Terrorism
Reagan lanza el programa Star Wars (SDI)

So the Reagan administration started developing an antimissile system in outerspace, the so-called Strategic Defense Initiative (SDI), more popularly known as 'Star Wars.' Critics of the program point out that 80 percent of the physicists, chemists, engineers, and mathematicians in the National Academy of Sciences oppose SDI; only 10 percent favor it.
The Arms Chase
Guerra contra de los contras devasta Nicaragua

As of 1986, the contra war in Nicaragua had claimed some 9,000 people and had left 7,200 children without parents. ... Assisted by US military advisors and hundreds of millions of dollars, the contras have conducted a war of attrition against the Nicaraguan people. ... they attacked health clinics, collective farms, agricultural cooperatives, croplands, schools and homes, indiscriminately killing men, women, and children.
The Mean Methods of Imperialism (II)
Gasto militar de Reagan rebasa dos billones de dólares

In eight years, his administration spent about two trillion (two thousand billion) dollars on defense, more than the combined defense expenditures of the Truman, Eisenhower, Kennedy, Johnson, Nixon, Ford, and Carter administrations. Yet in a June 1986 press conference, President Reagan claimed that the United States was still militarily inferior to the Soviet Union—leaving some observers to wonder how so much money could buy so little security.
